newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-LATE GOAL PUTS SPARTA PRAGUE THROUGH TO CUP 2ND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE GOAL PUTS SPARTA PRAGUE THROUGH TO CUP 2ND ROUND.

text.p: Sparta Prague advanced past Sturm Graz with a 1-1 win in their second leg Cup Winners' Cup match on Thursday, but only barely, scoring a late goal to come from behind.
After a 2-2 away tie in the first leg in Austria two weeks ago, Sparta needed to hold Sturm to a 1-1 tie or better to advance to the second round of the tournament.
With that in mind, the Czech cup winners played a cautious match, rarely allowing Sturm to control the ball inside their half of centre as the teams played to a scoreless half.
Sparta picked up the play in the second half, controlling the ball but failing to create many good scoring opportunities.

Then in the 76th minute, Sparta's most experienced defender Jiri Novotny did the unthinkable, knocking Ivica Vastic's weak shot past the outstretched hands of goalkeeper Ivan Ondruska to put Sturm ahead 1-0.

Sparta was then went on the offensive, creating several scoring chances before Zdenek Svoboda's cross found a closely marked Michal Hornak, who headed in his first European competition goal to even the game.
"We knew it would be a tough match and we showed a lot of character coming back in the final minutes. I believed all game we would advance, but not without a fight," said Sparta coach Josef Chovanec.
